We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template from make_8_lvl2-template_search-1 to the given molecule. We have the mapped_rxn and template_id from that prior step. The answer gave a JSON dict with mapped_rxn and template_id 12345 (example). We need to apply that template to the target molecule to get precursors.

We have the target SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

We need to retrieve the template SMARTS using get_template with template_id. Then apply_template to get precursors list. Then format as list of lists (each combination). Likely only one combination: sulfonyl chloride (phenylsulfonyl chloride) and amine? The reaction is sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide + HCl. So precursors: the amine (the aromatic amine part) and phenylsulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl). The target includes sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring with other substituents. The amine part is the N attached to aromatic ring (the N is part of sulfonamide). The amine precursor would be the aromatic amine (Ar-NH2?) Actually the target has N attached to sulfonyl group and to aromatic ring (the N is part of sulfonamide linking to aromatic ring). In retrosynthesis, break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and amine (Ar-NH2). The amine would be the aromatic amine that was originally attached to sulfonyl group. In the target, the N is attached to aromatic ring (the same ring). So the amine precursor is the same aromatic ring with NH2 (instead of sulfonamide). So we need to generate SMILES for that amine and for phenylsulfonyl chloride (maybe with same aryl group as sulfonyl part? The sulfonyl part is attached to a phenyl ring with fluorine substituent (C5=C(F)C=CC=C5). That's a phenyl ring with F. So phenylsulfonyl chloride would be O=S(Cl)(c1ccc(F)cc1). SMILES: O=S(Cl)c1ccc(F)cc1? Actually sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)Ar. SMILES: O=S(Cl)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1? The correct SMILES: O=S(Cl)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1? Wait typical: ClS(=O)(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1F. So SMILES: O=S(Cl)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1. Might need double O: O=S(Cl)(=O)?? Actually sulfonyl chloride has two double-bonded O: O=S(Cl)(=O)Ar. That's O=S(Cl)(=O)Ar. So SMILES: O=S(Cl)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1. Good.

The amine precursor: the aromatic amine part: the N attached to the aromatic ring (the same ring as the sulfonamide). The target aromatic ring is complex with many substituents. The amine would be the same ring but with NH2 instead of N-SO2... So we need to replace the N-SO2 group with NH2. The SMILES for that amine: c1... need to generate. The target SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

The N is attached to C1 of aromatic ring: NC1=CC(...). So the amine precursor would be N? Actually the amine is the aromatic amine: the aromatic ring with NH2 attached (maybe as -NH2). So SMILES: Nc1ccc(...). Need to reconstruct.

Simplify: The aromatic system is a fused polycyclic? Hard.

But we can rely on apply_template tool to compute precursors automatically. So we need to get template SMARTS first.

Let's call get_template with template_id from the dict: 12345 (string).
